es.thesis: Inquilinos y propietarios en bloques urbanos de España ya se prestan herramientas por el grupo de WhatsApp de la finca, con fricción, desconfianza y objetos que se pierden. Vecindario sería una app móvil (iOS y Android) por comunidad de vecinos: inventario compartido, reservas y reputación ligera, con un backend que aísla cada finca. El hueco no es que nadie lo haya intentado, sino una versión local, simple y por edificio frente a marketplaces de alquiler entre desconocidos.

idea.problem: Quien vive en un piso no quiere comprar un taladro que usa dos veces al año. El grupo de WhatsApp no tiene disponibilidad, depósito ni historial; prestarle algo a un vecino nuevo da miedo. Las apps de alquiler P2P asumen extraños, desplazamiento y comisión.
idea.solution: Un inventario cerrado al portal o la comunidad: alta de objetos, franja de reserva, recordatorio de devolución y un perfil mínimo de fiabilidad. Sin feed público ni matching a escala de ciudad en v1.
idea.who_primary: Residentes de fincas de 20-80 viviendas en ciudades españolas
idea.who_secondary: Presidentes de comunidad que quieren reducir compras duplicadas
idea.who_not: Alquiler profesional de maquinaria; campus universitarios (otro modelo de confianza)
idea.why_now: Los hábitos de segunda mano y usar en vez de poseer ya existen; WhatsApp es el apaño. No hay un incumbente español obvio por finca con buena UX móvil.
scope_in: Chat mínimo o enlace a WhatsApp

requirements.mobile: Must-have (v1): Android + iOS; auth email/Google; lista de objetos; ficha; calendario de reserva; mis préstamos; notificaciones de solicitud y atraso; estados vacío y error de red. Later: iPad, cola offline, pagos, OCR de fotos, widgets.
requirements.backend: Must-have (v1): tenant por community_id; users, items, bookings; auth; push (FCM/APNs); reglas de no solapar reservas; fotos en object storage; exportar y borrar cuenta. Later: pagos, moderación, analytics de producto, admin multi-finca.
requirements.cross_cutting: Copy en ES primero; analytics mínimo (altas, objetos, préstamos completados); cuenta GDPR; revisión de stores (fotos de usuarios).
requirements.score_why: Dos apps nativas, auth, push, fotos y aislamiento por tenant son un CRUD estándar, no un marketplace con pagos en v1.

competition.method: Búsquedas: app prestar herramientas vecinos, library of things Spain, Peerby, Fat Llama, alquiler herramientas particulares app. Páginas de producto. Fecha: 2026-09-08.

competitors.relevance: El análogo de producto más cercano, con otra frontera de confianza.

competition.positioning: Ganar en comunidad cerrada más calendario, no en oferta de ciudad. Si no conseguimos que un presidente o 8 vecinos listen 15 objetos, Peerby y WhatsApp ya cubren el trabajo.
competition.gap_verdict_text: Hay demanda del trabajo (conseguir un taladro sin comprarlo), pero el canal dominante es WhatsApp y los P2P de ciudad ya existen. Un producto por portal puede encajar si la distribución es la comunidad, no la store. No es un océano azul.
competition.score_why: Peerby y el grupo de WhatsApp ya hacen el trabajo; la apertura es solo este edificio, no una categoría vacía.

en.thesis: Tenants and owners in urban apartment buildings in Spain already lend tools via the building WhatsApp group, with friction, distrust, and items that go missing. Vecindario would be a mobile app (iOS and Android) per residents' community: shared inventory, bookings, and light reputation, with a backend that isolates each building. The gap is not that nobody has tried this; it is a local, simple, per-building version versus rental marketplaces for strangers.

idea.problem: Someone in a flat does not want to buy a drill they use twice a year. The WhatsApp group has no availability, deposit, or history; lending to a new neighbour feels risky. P2P rental apps assume strangers, travel, and a commission.
idea.solution: A closed inventory for the portal or community: list items, book a slot, return reminder, and a minimal reliability profile. No public feed and no city-wide matching in v1.
idea.who_primary: Residents of 20-80 unit buildings in Spanish cities
idea.who_secondary: Community presidents who want fewer duplicate purchases
idea.who_not: Professional equipment rental; university campuses (different trust model)
idea.why_now: Second-hand and use-instead-of-own habits already exist; WhatsApp is the workaround. There is no obvious Spanish per-building incumbent with good mobile UX.
scope_in: Minimal chat or WhatsApp deep link

requirements.mobile: Must-have (v1): Android + iOS; email/Google auth; item list; item detail; booking calendar; my loans; request and overdue notifications; empty and network-error states. Later: iPad, offline queue, payments, photo OCR, widgets.
requirements.backend: Must-have (v1): tenant per community_id; users, items, bookings; auth; push (FCM/APNs); no overlapping bookings; photos in object storage; export/delete account. Later: payments, moderation, product analytics, multi-building admin.
requirements.cross_cutting: Spanish copy first; minimal analytics (signups, items, completed loans); GDPR account; store review for user photos.
requirements.score_why: Two native apps, auth, push, photos, and tenant isolation are standard CRUD, not a payments marketplace in v1.

competition.method: Queries: neighbour tool lending app, library of things Spain, Peerby, Fat Llama, peer tool rental app. Fetched vendor pages. Date: 2026-09-08.

competitors.name: Peerby
competitors.strengths: Brand and liquidity in some markets.
competitors.weaknesses: Not designed as this building; city-scale cold start.
competitors.relevance: Closest product analog; different trust boundary.

competitors.name: Fat Llama and similar marketplaces
competitors.what: Rental with insurance and commission among strangers.
competitors.weaknesses: Overkill and pricey for a drill two floors up.

competitors.name: Building WhatsApp group
competitors.relevance: The product to beat on ease, not on features.

competition.positioning: Win on closed community plus calendar, not city-wide supply. If we cannot get a president or eight neighbours to list 15 items, Peerby and WhatsApp already cover the job.
competition.gap_verdict_text: Demand for the job (get a drill without buying one) exists, but WhatsApp is the dominant channel and city-wide P2P already exists. A per-portal product can fit if distribution is the community, not the store. This is not a blue ocean.
competition.score_why: Peerby-class P2P plus the WhatsApp group already do the job; the opening is only this building, not an empty category.

models.name: Community fee (B2B2C)
models.short_term: A president can approve a small expense.
models.why_score: A payer exists, but ARPU is tiny and the motion is sales-like.

models.name: Freemium + IAP building Pro
models.how: Limited inventory free; extra push and photos paid.
models.short_term: Almost nobody pays to lend a drill.
models.long_term: Consumer IAP against a free chat alternative.
models.why_score: Weak willingness to pay versus WhatsApp.

models.name: Take-rate or deposit
models.how: Like Fat Llama: insurance and charge per loan.
models.short_term: Kills the it is just the neighbour pitch.
models.long_term: Only if you leave the building and become a city marketplace.

monetization.recommended_v1: Do not charge until one building completes loans weekly. Then test a community fee (~10 EUR/month) with the president — not consumer IAP.
monetization.score_why: A community fee is plausible, but ARPU is small and the status quo is free; no strong short-term or compounding long-term path.

technical.text: Photos, push, and two stores. Mitigation: BaaS or a thin API first.
Scale: v1 is tiny; tenant isolation matters more than QPS.

product.text: Chicken-egg inside each building. Mitigation: seed 10 items with the president.
Nobody opens another app versus WhatsApp. Mitigation: WhatsApp deep links in v1.

market.text: Peerby and marketplaces absorb serious lenders.
Switching cost of the existing chat group is near zero.

legal.text: Damage or loss of items: disclaimers in v1, no insurance.
GDPR and indoor photos: retention and delete account.

business.text: Support for they did not return it does not scale.

risks.score_why: Per-building chicken-egg, WhatsApp inertia, unclear payer, and object-loss disputes are several High/Medium killers, not a polish problem.

action_plan.phase0: 10 conversations in 2 real buildings. Success: at least 4 people would list an item this week and the president would forward a link. Failure: we will talk about it in the group, with no pain.
action_plan.phase1: One pilot community, inventory + booking + push, no payments.
action_plan.phase2: Second building; completed loans per week; then iOS polish or waitlist.
next_14_days: Interview 8 neighbours and 1 president (last time they needed a tool).
Map 5 real alternatives with current URLs (including local ES).
Pretotype: shared sheet + WA group and measure 2 weeks.
Decide kill or wedge (tools only vs books and cables too).
Only if there is signal: sketch 4 screens and community/item/booking model.
action_plan.score_why: A thin v1 (one community, inventory, booking, push, no payments) is weeks for a small team after validation, not a multi-year build.

open_questions: Is the building administrator the distribution channel?
Does v1 allow open communities (friends) or only a portal code?
